assumptions: Red flashes were judged with the WCAG 2.2 working definition: one state has R/(R+G+B) >= 0.8 and the two states differ by more than 0.2 in CIE 1976 u'v' chromaticity (ADR-001).
The redness ratio R/(R+G+B) is computed on each 4x4 px cell's colour re-encoded to whole 0-255 sRGB values, and is 0 when R < 16: a red that dark has no visible hue (ADR-003, ADR-020).

notes: 3 animation(s) found at frame 0, 0 discovered later
2 SVG SMIL timeline(s) paused and set to the frame time
2 SVG timeline un-pause(s) by the page were undone
Math.random replaced by a fixed-seed generator (mulberry32, seed 0x2f6e2b1); crypto.getRandomValues is not seeded
document.timeline.currentTime reads the fake clock (performance.now()), not the real one
requestAnimationFrame callbacks run once per captured frame, at that frame's clock time
IntersectionObserver entries computed once per captured frame on that frame's layout and delivered in a task on the page clock (ADR-052)
fake clock stepped in whole ms: frame i sits at round((i + 0.25)*1000/60) ms, animations seeked to the exact time (ADR-029)
clock and double-shot checks at frame 0, every 60th frame and the last frame; uncontrollable content looked for again at every frame (CSS images at those checkpoints)

disclaimer: Analysis aid, not a compliance certification.

evidenceFrames.label: frame 12 (t = 0.200 s) - first qualifying general flash

fixes.rationale: The engine counted up to 5 flashes in one second in the general violation (its busiest one-second window, a whole count that can include a flash right on the window's edge). Stretching each iteration of 'strobe' from 200 ms to 400 ms (5 / 2.5 = 2.00 times longer) slows its flashes by that factor: evenly spaced flashes end up at least 0.4 s apart, so any one second holds at most 3, and WCAG 2.3.1 fails only content that "flashes more than three times in any one second period". Measured inside the element's box (per-pixel median): frame 11 rgb(20, 20, 20) (L 0.007, R/(R+G+B) 0.333), frame 12 rgb(255, 255, 255) (L 1.000, R/(R+G+B) 0.333).

fixes.css: @keyframes ft-fix-1-lum { 0% { background-color: #575757; animation-timing-function: steps(1); } 50% { background-color: rgb(20, 20, 20); animation-timing-function: steps(1); } 100% { background-color: #575757; animation-timing-function: steps(1); } } #loader { animation-name: ft-fix-1-lum !important; }
fixes.rationale: Lowers the brighter animated colour(s), keeping each hue (scaled in linear light, stored as sRGB hex): #ffffff (L 1.000) -> #575757 (L 0.095). The animated colours then differ by at most 0.088 in relative luminance, under the 0.10 of a general flash (WCAG: "a pair of opposing changes in relative luminance of 10% or more"). Measured inside the element's box (per-pixel median): frame 11 rgb(20, 20, 20) (L 0.007, R/(R+G+B) 0.333), frame 12 rgb(255, 255, 255) (L 1.000, R/(R+G+B) 0.333).

fixes.css: /* not auto-applied: changes layout */ #loader { transform: scale(0.402); transform-origin: top left; }
fixes.rationale: 7588 of the element's 4x4 px cells flashed; a flash qualifies only above 1360 cells (WCAG: "25% of any 10 degree visual field"). Scaling the element by 0.402 (sqrt(1360 / 7588) x 0.95) brings it below that. Not applied automatically: an area fix changes the page layout, so FlashTrace never verifies it by re-capture. Measured inside the element's box (per-pixel median): frame 11 rgb(20, 20, 20) (L 0.007, R/(R+G+B) 0.333), frame 12 rgb(255, 255, 255) (L 1.000, R/(R+G+B) 0.333).

limitations: Headless sRGB rendering is not a physical display; brightness, gamma and viewing distance differ per user.
Canvas/WebGL attribution is element-level only (what is drawn inside cannot be attributed).
Cross-origin iframes are unattributable and cannot be clock-controlled.
Animated GIF/WebP/APNG, animated SVG images and Web Workers force non-deterministic capture (strategy C) and a PASS becomes INCONCLUSIVE.
Under realtime capture (strategy C) a measured rate can be one flash per second higher or lower than the page's, because a compositor frame drawn late or dropped moves a transition by one frame.

Under strategy A, work that the page starts and the browser finishes on the real clock is not waited for (ADR-052): React scheduler tasks (MessageChannel messages), the page's handling of `fetch` and `XMLHttpRequest` answers, history traversals (`history.back()`, `forward()`, `go()`), script, style and image load events, `window.postMessage`, WebSocket and EventSource messages, storage callbacks and Navigation API traversals. A page that changes what it shows on such an event can show that change one frame earlier or later in another capture (several frames when the page also holds the change behind a gate on its own timers), although both captures are reported as deterministic.

Under strategy A, IntersectionObserver is FlashTrace's own implementation (ADR-052). It clips a target by its ancestors' overflow along an approximated containing-block chain and ignores transforms, `clip-path`, `clip`, `border-radius`, `overflow-clip-margin` and `scrollMargin`, so a reveal that depends on those can start at a different scroll position than in a browser; `isVisible` (`trackVisibility`) equals `isIntersecting`, without an occlusion test.
The fine-pattern exception (T6) and spatial-pattern hazards are not evaluated.
Only the captured viewport and duration are analysed; content revealed by scrolling or interaction is analysed only if an interaction script drives it.
Window size for viewports other than 1024 px wide is scaled by the width ratio (an assumption).
The 341×256 px window is scored in whole 4×4 px cells and slides in 4 px steps, so a flashing area wider or taller than the window can be under-measured by up to 3 px along such an edge.
No numbers in this repository are estimates: accuracy, agreement and runtime figures exist only in `docs/RESULTS.md`, produced by `flashtrace bench`, with date and commit hash.
Math.random was replaced by a fixed-seed generator for this capture, but crypto.getRandomValues was not, so content driven by it may differ between runs (ADR-022).
Flashing faster than 30 per second (half the 60 fps capture rate) cannot be seen in the frames (ADR-019).
reason: General flashes reached 5 per second in a 341x256 px window at frames 0-359; WCAG 2.3.1 allows at most 3.
